name: blender_verify
description: Check a result by measurement. criteria: your own acceptance checks, each measured on the evaluated scene at its frames and passed or failed with the measured value. visible: whether an object shows in the render at a frame, otherwise every reason found (out of frame, hidden in render, collection excluded, view layer not rendered, holdout, transparent or zero-density material, no geometry, hidden behind another object). Render (the default without criteria or visible, or with render or view): low-resolution frames with facts (black or transparent, brightness, the camera used and why, sequencer, compositing, instances). geometry: what is wrong with the meshes in view (inward normals, open or non-manifold edges, zero-area faces, coplanar overlapping faces between objects); a render names its near-black areas and the object there. caches: simulation caches the checked frames read without a current bake (not baked, outdated, frames outside); unsaved: the file lacks changes you checked here. Settings, cameras and the current frame are restored; the revision stays.

criteria.description: Up to 50 checks: {expr: a read-only Python expression, or path: from bpy.data; op: < <= > >= == != approx between in contains; value; frame or frames (default: the call's); tol (approx, default 1e-4); label}. In expr: bounds(name).min.z (world bounds of the evaluated geometry), ev(name) (evaluated object), world(name), scene, frame, bpy, Vector, math. Vectors compare element by element.

visible.description: {object, frame or frames}: does it show in the render, and why not.

saved.description: true: read the open file as saved on disk (a background Blender opens it; same criteria, visible and render), or a .blend path. Compare it with the open document.

render.description: Also render (default: only without criteria and visible).

scene.description: Default: the active scene. The facts say which scene was read (scene, scene_read) and warn when it is a shot shown by another scene's montage.

frames.description: 1 to 16 frames, as one contact sheet (instead of frame).

view.description: {location: [x, y, z], target: [x, y, z] or an object name or {object, bone}, lens?: mm (default 50)}: render from a free viewpoint, world space.

size.description: Longest side of each image in pixels (64 to 640; a sheet stays within 1280).
